declared_purpose: Read-only Figma inspection, design-system and accessibility analysis, asset export, and documentation/report generation. Remote design modification is explicitly excluded. These capabilities do not explicitly require repeated retrievals, design-text inclusion in typography results, or image-URL persistence (SKILL.md:3–16, 23–49, 150–165).

data_operations.operation: Read authentication credentials locally and attach them to API requests
data_operations.source: Constructor argument, FIGMA_ACCESS_TOKEN environment variable, or figma_client.py --token argument
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: FigmaClient configuration and requests.Session memory; X-Figma-Token header sent to https://api.figma.com/v1
data_operations.condition: Client construction requires a token. Other scripts use the environment-based constructor.
Only if the user follows the optional shell recipe. The Python constructor reads the environment; no .env loader is shown.

data_operations.source: Caller-supplied file key, node IDs and optional parameters
data_operations.data_scope: Outbound identifiers and query parameters; inbound file document, components, styles and metadata, or selected-node responses
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Identifiers and credentials go to Figma API; response JSON returns to the calling process
data_operations.condition: get_file or get_file_nodes invocation. The wrapper supports parameters, but audit and general export paths request complete files without scope parameters.

data_operations.source: Explicit wrapper-method calls or get-components/get-styles CLI commands
data_operations.data_scope: File versions, image-fill metadata, components, styles, team projects, project files and team libraries; associated resource identifiers
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Figma API receives identifiers and authentication; response JSON stays with the caller unless subsequently output
data_operations.condition: Only the applicable method or CLI branch runs; these methods are not automatic prerequisites for every analysis.

data_operations.source: get_user_info method or user-info CLI command
data_operations.data_scope: Authenticated account response; exact returned fields are not established by this source
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Authenticated GET to Figma API /me; response returns to caller or CLI output handling
data_operations.condition: Explicit invocation only; no automatic account lookup is shown.

data_operations.data_scope: Colors, typography, node identifiers and names; typography extraction additionally copies complete text-node characters
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: In-process result lists returned to caller; CLI may print or save them
data_operations.condition: extract_colors, extract_text_styles, extract-colors or extract-typography invocation

data_operations.operation: Infer design-quality attributes and aggregate findings locally
data_operations.source: File nodes, fills, typography, bounds, effects and names; configured brand colors and fonts
data_operations.data_scope: Contrast estimates, inferred interactive/focus status, brand and consistency findings, node references, scores and compliance labels; multi-file summaries
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Checker results and StyleAuditor memory, then caller
data_operations.condition: Requested audit path and enabled checks; brand checks require configured guidelines. These are design assessments, not observations of actual users.

data_operations.operation: Read a local list of audit targets
data_operations.data_scope: Nonempty stripped lines interpreted as file keys or URLs
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local process; parsed keys subsequently drive authenticated Figma requests
data_operations.condition: audit-multiple and os.path.isfile succeeds; otherwise the argument is split on commas.

data_operations.data_scope: Complete result JSON, potentially including complete file data, design text, account metadata or export URLs according to the command
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Standard output by default; caller-selected local --output file otherwise
data_operations.condition: Successful CLI command. A normal library return has no additional persistence here.

data_operations.data_scope: File identifiers and names, timestamps, issue details, node references, scores, recommendations and cross-file summaries; HTML includes file name and issue summaries
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Standard output or local --output JSON file; optional local HTML report
data_operations.condition: Successful audit-file/audit-multiple; CLI HTML generation additionally requires --generate-html and audit-file.

data_operations.data_scope: File key/name, timestamp, scores, issue node IDs/names and measurements; text smaller than 12px additionally contributes its first 50 characters
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Standard output or selected local JSON file; local HTML file for HTML mode, including issue details
data_operations.condition: Requested accessibility check; snippet collection occurs only for text below the minimum size. HTML mode writes a report even without --output.

data_operations.source: Selected export nodes and configured formats/scales
data_operations.data_scope: File key, node IDs, format and scale sent remotely; image URLs returned
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Figma API /images/{file_key}; response stays with caller or export manager
data_operations.condition: export-images CLI or export-manager asset paths. Export manager requests each node/format/scale combination separately.

data_operations.source: API-returned image URL, or explicit download_image argument
data_operations.data_scope: URL requested remotely and returned image bytes
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Host identified by image_url; bytes written to local output_path, normally under configured export directories
data_operations.condition: A nonempty image URL exists and the export is not skipped. Download uses standalone requests.get, not the token-bearing client session.

data_operations.operation: Return export metadata and persist a manifest
data_operations.data_scope: Local paths, node IDs/names, formats, scales and image URLs; manifest adds file key, export time and configuration
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Result returned to caller; local export-manifest.json under the current output directory
data_operations.condition: Manifest persistence defaults to enabled; library configuration can disable it. Returning the metadata alone does not establish remote disclosure.

data_operations.source: Complete retrieved file; extraction consumes its styles map
data_operations.data_scope: Style-derived names and identifiers, placeholder color/typography/effect values, and fixed spacing values
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local design-tokens.json/css/scss/js in configured output directory
data_operations.condition: export-tokens or client-package. Several values are placeholders, not measured design attributes.

data_operations.operation: Build a local client package and source documentation
data_operations.data_scope: All frames/components, token files and README containing file name/key, last-modified value, version and export time
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local package directory; no automatic client delivery is implemented
data_operations.condition: client-package invocation. It repeats file retrieval through its suboperations and documentation helper.

data_operations.data_scope: File keys, node names, output paths, request/resource URLs and exception text, depending on the path
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Standard output or standard error; external capture is not established
data_operations.condition: Applicable progress, retry or error branch. Explicit token logging is not shown.

potential_excess.data_scope: Complete text-node characters included alongside typography attributes
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: extract_text_styles caller; extract-typography standard output or selected local JSON file
potential_excess.condition: Typography extraction where the requested outcome is font/style information rather than text content
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Typography analysis requires style attributes and node references; copying all text is an implementation choice.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Extract the requested typography attributes and identify their source nodes.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Omit the text field by default; include text only for an explicitly requested content/sample-text outcome. This removes extra result data from a required extraction.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain font metrics, node IDs and sufficient labels for locating styles.

potential_excess.data_scope: First 50 characters of text nodes smaller than 12px
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Accessibility result returned to caller, printed JSON, selected JSON file, or generated HTML issue details
potential_excess.condition: A text node fails the minimum-size check
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The size determination uses fontSize; design text is not used to calculate the failure.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Report the undersized node, measured size and threshold.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Remove characters from default issue details or make excerpts opt-in. Keep the required finding and report.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve node ID/name, severity and size measurements so the issue remains actionable.

potential_excess.data_scope: Complete file document and unrelated node content retrieved for token generation
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Figma API response entering ExportManager process memory
potential_excess.condition: export_design_tokens, including each client-package token-format invocation
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Current extraction consumes the styles map and fixed spacing values; it does not inspect the document tree.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Obtain equivalent style names, types and identifiers for token generation.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Use a narrower style-metadata request where equivalent, or the minimum file scope that retains required style metadata. This narrows data in a required retrieval.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Verify the narrower response supplies all identifiers and metadata consumed by the existing extractors; preserve requested output formats.

potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Complete Figma file response entering ExportManager process memory
potential_excess.condition: Library export_frames call with explicit frame_ids and no frame-name selection
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Exporting identified frames requires their metadata and rendering, while the implementation retrieves and traverses the entire file first.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Validate and identify the requested frames, then export them with configured settings.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Retrieve scoped node metadata for the explicit IDs, following the existing custom-selection approach. Retain broader discovery when selecting by name or requesting all frames.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve frame-type validation, names, selection semantics and configured export outputs.

potential_excess.data_scope: Repeated complete-file requests and responses during one client-package build
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Repeated authenticated requests to Figma API /files/{file_key} and repeated responses into local process memory
potential_excess.condition: Successful package path makes six complete-file calls with package_name supplied, or seven without it, excluding retries
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The package requires frames, components, several token formats and documentation; separate retrievals for the same file are an implementation choice.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Acquire sufficient design data to create the complete requested package.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Retrieve one file snapshot and reuse it for naming, frame/component selection, token serialization and README generation. This removes redundant actions rather than merely trimming response fields.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep every requested asset and token format; use a consistent snapshot and avoid introducing persistent caching.

potential_excess.data_scope: API-returned image URLs retained after asset download
potential_excess.condition: Successful asset exports with create_manifest enabled, which is the default
potential_excess.purpose_basis: An organized export manifest can describe downloaded assets without preserving their remote download URLs.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Persist the requested assets and useful inventory metadata.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Omit URL fields from the persisted manifest by default or make their retention explicit. This narrows a manifest's contents; it does not require removing the manifest or normal caller return.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain local paths, node references, formats, scales and counts needed for handoff.

potential_excess.data_scope: File key, node ID, format, scale and authentication sent for an export that will be skipped
potential_excess.condition: Library configuration sets skip_existing=True and the computed output file already exists
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Skipping an existing local asset does not require a fresh rendering request.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Determine the expected local path and preserve the existing file.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Compute the filename and check local existence before export_images. This removes a redundant remote action.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve naming, directory organization, skip behavior and handling of exports whose files do not exist.

unknowns: Figma's server-side access logging, retention, deletion and internal processing are not established by the supplied source.

Actual download hosts and URL access semantics depend on runtime API responses. The downloader does not constrain the host; external behavior beyond its GET and local write remains unresolved (scripts/figma_client.py:161–169).
Runtime file contents, credential permissions, selected commands and caller-side handling of returned data are unknown. A normal return does not establish further disclosure.

No retention schedule or cleanup/deletion implementation is shown for generated assets, manifests, token files, reports or optional .env storage. Filesystem protections and subsequent sharing are unknown.

Report generators interpolate design-derived strings into HTML without escaping. Any additional browser behavior depends on actual content and report viewing; no concrete additional recipient can be established (scripts/accessibility_checker.py:478–492; scripts/style_auditor.py:678–688).

Reference recommendations concerning external tools, caching, audit logs or deployment do not establish executed integrations. The packaged template and dependency declarations do not establish additional data flows.

Advertised document-components and dev-handoff workflows are absent from the corresponding CLI command choices; audit-brand is accepted but has no execution branch. Their advertised outcomes have no implemented data flow to audit (SKILL.md:123–148; scripts/figma_client.py:229–233; scripts/export_manager.py:498–510; scripts/style_auditor.py:710–711, 733–749).
